question: Can each mind keep its own life memory and a signed history of the lessons that held up, and pass a distilled slice of only those lessons to a bred child — so that memory beats no memory on repeat-domain work, and a child with inherited lessons beats the same child bred without them — while no raw personal content is ever inherited and a deletion removes a memory completely?
why: Simon's spec, 2026-10-28, UPGRADE 2 (per-mind memory and inherited history), built third. Inspired by Gary W. Floyd's NexusGrid as he described it in chat (Gary W. Floyd, Lumiea Systems Research Division — ThunderStruck Service LLC); designed from that description only — no parity with his system is claimed; the comparison follows his catch-up call. Breeding minds is Master Vision step 6, owned by the Master Vision session (kardlings / living-seed organ 5); this organ supplies the memory and inheritance a mind card carries, keyed by its genome hash.
honesty: Minds are MODELS of thought-patterns — small predictive models of an outcome — never the people in the data and never claimed conscious.

The five datasets carry no free text. To test that no personal content is inherited, every episode carries a PLANTED note with a unique canary token standing in for what a person might have said; the canaries are synthetic, the rows are real.
A lesson is a fact about the world (an outcome rate in a cell of the data), not a copy of a case; a child turns it into its own correction.

data.what: The same five real public datasets and loaders as organ 2 (vendor/dex-frontier/SOURCES.json, pinned).
data.rows: From each dataset's first 6,000 FIT rows: founders = rows 0–799; life = rows 800–5,999. Repeat-domain and early-life tasks are TEST rows (the first 6,000), read only by the measurement after every life is over.

design.minds: Per dataset two parents. Genes = an organ of raw feature specs, logistic, fitted as organ 2's model: parent A on founder rows 0–399 with the features at even positions, parent B on founder rows 400–799 with the features at odd positions. A mind's id = SHA-256 of its canonical genes (the genome hash a mind card names). Each mind has its own Ed25519 key from the phrase 'watch-dream-remember/mind/<id>'.
design.segment: Per dataset the segment feature s = the raw feature with the largest |β| in a fit of all raw features on founder rows 0–799; A lives on life rows with s ≤ its FIT median, B on rows with s > it.
design.life: A parent's life: its segment's life rows, in order, in batches of 200, at most 10 batches. Each case is an EPISODE in its life memory: the row's values, the outcome, a planted note 'note <dataset>:<row> <canary>' (canary: 12 hex characters from mulberry32(20261029 + 3)), a per-episode random salt, and provenance { mind, batch, ref = HMAC-SHA-256(salt, row) }.
design.lessons: Cells: for the mind’s 4 strongest features (|β|), each of the 6 pairs × 4 quadrants by FIT medians = 24 cells. A lesson for a cell = { cell, context, rate = (k + 1)/(n + 2), n } over the episodes in it, where context = the segment the mind lived in { f: s, side } (a child, which has no life yet, has no context of its own). A mind APPLIES a lesson only to a case in the lesson’s cell AND context: logit += the mean over such lessons with n ≥ 20 and ≥ 5 of the mind’s own founder cases in that cell and context, of w·(logit(rate) − logit(the mind’s mean founder prediction there)), w = n/(n + 50).
design.cycle: The mini daydream/dream after each batch: the daydream updates candidate lessons from the batch (inert); the dream VERIFIES — a lesson is verified when, over the batches after the one it was first formed in, applying it (as it stood before each batch) lowered the log-loss of its cell's cases in total, over at least 30 later cases. Only verified lessons are used at work and only verified lessons can be inherited.
design.history: Signed (the mind's key), hash-chained, append-only: one 'outcome' entry per batch { batch, n, logloss with and without its lessons }, one 'lesson' entry per verified lesson { cell, rate, n, gain }, an 'inherited' entry at birth { lessons, lineage }, and a 'tombstone' per deletion { count } — never an episode, a row, a note, a salt or a ref.
design.store: Life memory (episodes and lessons) is kept in LIGHT (fall-kit's vendored codec); the history is kept as JSON lines.
design.breeding: Genes = the gated fusion of both parents' patterns: the union of their specs, refitted on founder rows 0–799; born only if its GATE log-loss is below both parents'; otherwise the parent with the lower GATE log-loss gives its genes (recorded). Inherited history = a distilled slice: from each parent, its verified lessons, the top 8 by gain, each as { cell, context, rate, n, gain, lineage: [parent id] }. The child's own life memory starts empty.
design.deletion: delete(ids): the episodes and their salts leave the life memory, the LIGHT store is re-encoded from what remains, the lessons are recomputed from the remaining episodes, and one tombstone is appended.

claims.claim: Life memory beats no memory on repeat-domain tasks.
claims.pass: for each of the 10 parents, on the first 2,000 TEST rows of its own segment: log-loss with its verified lessons is at least 0.001 nats lower than the same genes without them, with the 95% paired bootstrap lower bound of the improvement above 0 (1,000 resamples, mulberry32(20261029 + 4)) — for at least 8 of the 10

claims.claim: A child with inherited lessons beats one bred without them, from the same parents.
claims.pass: for each of the 5 datasets, on the child's early life — the first 2,000 TEST rows — the child with the inherited slice is at least 0.001 nats lower in log-loss than the same child (same genes) bred without it, bootstrap lower bound above 0 — for at least 4 of the 5

claims.claim: No raw personal content is inherited, and a deletion fully removes a memory.
claims.pass: (a) every byte each child holds (genes, inherited slice, history, its empty life memory as LIGHT) contains none of its parents' canaries and no parent row's full list of values, and every inherited lesson has exactly the fields cell, context, rate, n, gain, lineage; (b) deleting 25 seeded episodes from each parent: none of their canaries remains anywhere in that parent's state (life memory LIGHT bytes, lessons, history), its lessons equal a fresh computation from the remaining episodes exactly, its history gains one tombstone and nothing else, and a child bred after the deletion inherits exactly the slice computed without them

predictions: Written before any memory code. M1: founders are only 400 rows, so cell rates learnt over up to 2,000 life cases should correct the genes where they are miscalibrated; gains small (0.001–0.01 nats) and not everywhere — 8 of 10 is a real bar. M2: each parent's slice covers its own segment, so the child, working across both, gets corrections it could not have; likely in 4 of 5. M3 by construction; the likeliest failure is a forgotten copy (a cache) still holding a deleted note.
disclosure: Superseded before any real data was read. A dry run of the measuring tool on SYNTHETIC datasets (WDR_SYNTH=1; no real row read) showed a flaw in v1’s rule: a parent lives in one segment, but its lesson about a cell was applied to the whole cell — both segments — so a child would carry a correction learnt on one half of the population onto the other half. v2 adds the context a lesson was learnt in (the parent’s segment) to the lesson itself; nothing else changes — the claims, bars, rows, seeds and the other rules are v1’s. The synthetic dry run’s numbers are not evidence and are not reported.
